title: Learned vs handcrafted adaptive restart for Nesterov on quadratics and logistic regression
setting: Each run draws random convex quadratics (dimension 20, spectrum exactly in [1, kappa]) or 12 row-subsamples of standardized load_breast_cancer logistic regression, with the L2 weight set so that L/mu is about kappa. Nesterov's method with FISTA momentum uses a restart rule that is either the O'Donoghue-Candes gradient rule with a grid-tuned threshold, a learned 2-parameter sigmoid policy (threshold and sharpness) fit by backpropagating a smoothed log-residual surrogate through a 40-step unrolled trajectory on 64 training quadratics, or no restart. The metric is the median iteration count until the noise-free gradient norm falls below 1e-6 of its initial value (capped at 5000), reported over 200 held-out quadratics or 12 logistic subsamples, with optional gradient noise relative to the gradient norm.

paper.title: Learning to Restart: Differentiable Restart Policies for Optimization Dynamics
paper.claim: A restart policy learned with differentiable surrogate gradients through the restart event needs fewer iterations to reach a target accuracy than the handcrafted gradient-based adaptive restart rule, and this advantage transfers zero-shot from synthetic quadratics to logistic regression.

metric.name: iters_median
metric.description: Median over held-out instances of the number of iterations until ||grad f(y_k)|| <= 1e-6 * ||grad f(x_0)||, where the gradient is noise-free at the query point. Instances that never reach the tolerance count as 5000. min_effect is 10 iterations.

factors.name: method
factors.description: odc_gradient is the O'Donoghue-Candes gradient restart rule (restart when grad·Δx > 0), with its threshold grid-tuned on the same training quadratics. learned_restart is the paper method: a sigmoid restart policy with threshold and sharpness fit by surrogate gradients on the same training quadratics, evaluated at the final temperature. no_restart is plain accelerated gradient as a reference.

factors.name: condition_number
factors.description: Condition number kappa of the training and test quadratics. For logistic regression it sets L/mu of the regularized objective through the L2 weight, so the conditioning regime is comparable across families.

factors.name: problem_family_transfer
factors.description: Test family. The learned and tuned policies are always fit on synthetic quadratics only, so the logistic level is a zero-shot transfer test on real data.

factors.name: gradient_noise
factors.description: Relative gradient noise: the gradient used for updates and restart scores is g + sigma·|g|·xi/sqrt(d) with standard normal xi. The convergence check uses the noise-free gradient.
